सुकेश चंद्रशेखर और Netflix के बीच छिड़ी कानूनी जंग में अब सरकार की एंट्री हो चुकी है! 🎬

दिल्ली की मंडोली जेल में बंद सुकेश चंद्रशेखर की डॉक्यूमेंट्री Love, Scam aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story 18 December 2026 को OTT प्लेटफॉर्म पर रिलीज़ होने वाली है। लेकिन सुकेश के वकील अनंत मलिक की अर्ज़ी के बाद यह मामला काफी गरमा गया है।

सुकेश की लीगल टीम का आरोप है कि पेंडिंग मुकदमों के बीच डॉक्यूमेंट्री रिलीज़ होने से उनके केस और फेयर ट्रायल के अधिकार पर गलत असर पड़ सकता है। इस शिकायत पर संज्ञान लेते हुए सूचना और प्रसारण मंत्रालय के उप निदेशक क्षितिज अग्रवाल ने 27 November 2026 को पत्र भेजकर Netflix से 7 दिनों में जवाब मांगा है।

रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, IT Rules 2021 के तहत यह नोटिस भेजा गया है। हालांकि, मंत्रालय ने फिलहाल Netflix को शो रोकने या टालने का कोई आदेश नहीं दिया है, सिर्फ उनका पक्ष मांगा है।

क्या पेंडिंग कोर्ट केस के दौरान ऐसी true-crime डॉक्यूमेंट्रीज़ रिलीज़ होनी चाहिए? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में ज़रूर दें! 🚨

ctx.text:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has sought a response from Netflix over its upcoming documentary, Love, Scam aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story, which is scheduled to premiere on December 18, 2026. The communication follows a representation filed on behalf of Chandrashekhar, raising concerns about the documentary's release while criminal proceedings against him are ongoing.
In a communication dated November 27, 2026, the Ministry forwarded the representation submitted by Advocate Anant Malik to Netflix Entertainment Services India and asked the streaming platform to examine the issues raised in it. The Ministry has sought Netflix's comments within seven days of receiving the communication.
The letter, bearing reference number J-11013/19/2025-DM, refers to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, and other applicable Indian laws. It also draws attention to the Code of Ethics governing digital news publishers and OTT platforms, which provides for a three-tier mechanism to address grievances concerning violations of the prescribed framework.
The Ministry further noted that OTT platforms are required not to transmit content prohibited by law and to exercise due caution and discretion. The communication was signed by Kshitij Aggarwal, Deputy Director (Digital Media), and issued with the approval of the competent authority.
The representation was submitted by Malik on behalf of Chandrashekhar, who is currently in judicial custody at Mandoli Jail in Delhi. It raises objections to the documentary being released before the conclusion of the criminal trials involving him.
As reported earlier, Chandrashekhar's legal team had also issued a notice to Netflix and other parties associated with the documentary, seeking a postponement of its release until prosecution evidence in the pending cases is concluded. The notice raised concerns about the portrayal of allegations that are yet to be tested in court and the potential impact on the right to a fair trial.
Importantly, the Ministry's latest communication does not direct Netflix to stop, postpone or withdraw the documentary. It has asked the platform to respond to the representation within the stipulated period. Netflix's response and the Ministry's subsequent course of action are awaited.
The development comes amid growing scrutiny of how true-crime documentaries portray individuals facing ongoing criminal proceedings, particularly in relation to the presumption of innocence and the right to a fair trial.
